searchText: <@!296630428754771968> that sounds like it's in the "good news" realm. At our weekly call tomorrow I want to start mapping out next steps for the state network, probably with some focus on the network component itself and how we model the network. So address by path, and this dramatically simplifies removing ~~unused~~ unreachable state? Yes, it allows for garbage collection that doesn't require refcounting That is good news! Does that also reduce round trips while looking something up in the trie? I don't think so, since we are addressing by `(path, node_hash)` which doesn't allow you to *jump* down into the trie since you won't know the hash of the node... and if we remove `node_hash` then we run into problems with de-duplicating data that is present in multiple state roots.... Oh, another thing for us to look at... How would migrating to Verkle Tries effect our plans. So I actually think that because each node is so wide, you probably can't practically store them in the current immutable-data-structure style, unless you make a base-16 overlay over them; you would probably have to just store the tree in-place Which is not that hard, there's a PoC: https://github.com/ethereum/research/blob/master/generic_in_place_tree/tree.py Can you explain what you mean by "each node is so wide" Each node in a verkle tree has 256 members (or possibly more, witnesses get a bit smaller if you go up to 2048) got it, so the individual "nodes" are just large yeah And you don't actually _want_ to give people these nodes Unless you're passing down the whole state You want to give people a proof, and a proof just requires a short chain of commitments plus the proof object so at present, to walk down into the trie, you'd fetch all the nodes along the path, which currently in the hexary patricia trie means getting up to 15 "extra" sibling node hashes per node you retrieve. IIUC, in the Verkle world, that would mean getting at worst 255 "extra" sibling node hashes per node if we did it the "naive" way And you're saying that the "better" way would be each node would come back with a "committment + proof" that only contains the node at the index we are drilling down through (eliminating the extra 1-255 sibling nodes)? by fetch you mean from the network or the DB? from the DB you can't avoid fetching siblings, but then again, page sizes are 4 kB anyway from the network, the better way would be to have an explicit method to fetch the commitment+proof directly Cool, still filling in large swaths of knowledge gaps for Verkle stuff, this helps

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content:
<@!296630428754771968> that sounds like it's in the "good news" realm.

At our weekly call tomorrow I want to start mapping out next steps for the state network, probably with some focus on the network component itself and how we model the network.

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: So address by path, and this dramatically simplifies removing ~~unused~~ unreachable state?

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Yes, it allows for garbage collection that doesn't require refcounting

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: That is good news!

excerpts.author: samwilsn
excerpts.content: Does that also reduce round trips while looking something up in the trie?

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: I don't think so, since we are addressing by `(path, node_hash)` which doesn't allow you to *jump* down into the trie since you won't know the hash of the node...

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: and if we remove `node_hash` then we run into problems with de-duplicating data that is present in multiple state roots....

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Oh, another thing for us to look at...  How would migrating to Verkle Tries effect our plans.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: So I actually think that because each node is so wide, you probably can't practically store them in the current immutable-data-structure style, unless you make a base-16 overlay over them; you would probably have to just store the tree in-place

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Which is not that hard, there's a PoC: https://github.com/ethereum/research/blob/master/generic_in_place_tree/tree.py

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Can you explain what you mean by "each node is so wide"

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Each node in a verkle tree has 256 members (or possibly more, witnesses get a bit smaller if you go up to 2048)

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: got it, so the individual "nodes" are just large

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: yeah

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: And you don't actually _want_ to give people these nodes

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Unless you're passing down the whole state

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: You want to give people a proof, and a proof just requires a short chain of commitments plus the proof object

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content:
so at present, to walk down into the trie, you'd fetch all the nodes along the path, which currently in the hexary patricia trie means getting up to 15 "extra" sibling node hashes per node you retrieve.

IIUC, in the Verkle world, that would mean getting at worst 255 "extra" sibling node hashes per node if we did it the "naive" way

And you're saying that the "better" way would be each node would come back with a "committment + proof" that only contains the node at the index we are drilling down through (eliminating the extra 1-255 sibling nodes)?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: by fetch you mean from the network or the DB?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: from the DB you can't avoid fetching siblings, but then again, page sizes are 4 kB anyway

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: from the network, the better way would be to have an explicit method to fetch the commitment+proof directly

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Cool, still filling in large swaths of knowledge gaps for Verkle stuff, this helps
